Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

moment noun

a very short time

also instant, a moment, for a moment

classical

Liv. 21.14.3: mōmentō cēpit (Lewis & Short)
Hor. S. 1.1.7–8: hōrae mōmentō (Lewis & Short)

mōmentum, mōmentī n.

noun, second declension

a moment, an instant

Mostly in the ablative: mōmentō temporis, in a moment (see in a moment); hōrae mōmentō, in the space of an hour.

Other words

  • pūnctum temporis — an instant

    also used · classical · Cic. Sest. 53: pūnctō temporis eōdem (Lewis & Short); Caes. BC 2.25: temporis pūnctō (Lewis & Short)

    nē pūnctum quidem temporis, not for a moment (Cic. Phil. 8.20, Lewis & Short).

  • paulisper — for a moment, for a little while

    adverb · also used · classical · Plaut. As. 5.2.30: paulisper manē (Lewis & Short); Gell. 19.1.17: paulisper movērī; Traupman 87: wait a minute, manē paulisper

Examples

  • Manē paulisper.

    Wait a moment.Traupman 87

  • sapientis quoque animum paulisper movērī et contrahī et pallēscere necessum est

    even a wise man’s mind is bound to be shaken for a moment, to shrink and to turn paleGell. 19.1.17

See also in a moment, wait a moment!, just now, moment, minute.
